description: Background refresh and local notifications (mobile-apps spec 'Notifications without remote push'). The refresh reads GET /api/v1/notifications?unread=true&sort=-createdAt&pageSize=50 and compares each item's createdAt with the cursor saved on the device (the newest createdAt already seen).
rules: New = unread items whose createdAt is strictly later than the cursor.
No cursor yet (first refresh after sign-in) = nothing is new; the cursor is set to the newest createdAt.
The cursor always moves to the newest createdAt in the response, whether or not a notification is posted. It never moves backwards.
The notification text contains no personal data: only the count. Tapping it opens the approvals inbox when any new item has category 'approvals', otherwise the notifications inbox.
When the user turned local notifications off, nothing is posted (the cursor still moves).
Android schedules the refresh with WorkManager at the minimum interval of 15 minutes, requiring a network connection; iOS uses BGAppRefreshTask (the OS decides the timing).

serverCursor.description: Servers from Nov 2026 add an opaque `cursor` to every GET /api/v1/notifications response (task 1.2). Prefer it; the createdAt cases below remain the rule for older servers whose response has no `cursor` field.
rules: First refresh after sign-in (nothing stored): GET /api/v1/notifications?pageSize=1 and store its `cursor`; post nothing.

Later refreshes: GET /api/v1/notifications?since=<stored>&pageSize=50 returns only newer items, oldest first, with `cursor` pointing at the last item returned; repeat with that cursor until `items` is empty (the apps stop after 10 pages).
Count the returned items with readAt null; the text, opens and notifications-off rules are the same as above. Store the last cursor even when nothing is posted.
Opening the notifications inbox stores the `cursor` of that list response (no since), so items already seen are not announced later.
Android stores the server cursor prefixed with 'srv:' to tell it apart from a createdAt value; that prefix is a storage detail, not part of the contract.
